meta.name: The Best Off-Leash Dog Parks in the East Bay
meta.title_tag: Best Off-Leash Dog Parks in the East Bay
meta.excerpt: We started with every East Bay dog park that has at least 100 Google reviews, kept the ones rated 4.3 stars or higher, ranked them by rating, and verified each park's dog rules against its official city or park-district page in July 2026. Here are the twelve that made the cut, from Point Isabel in Richmond to the Marina in San Leandro.
meta.meta_description: The 12 best off-leash dog parks in the East Bay, from Richmond to the Tri-Valley — ranked by Google rating, with dog rules verified July 2026.

hero.alt: Point Isabel Regional Shoreline — from Wooffy's Bay Area dog guide (photo: Clyde Charles Brown, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons)

body_html:
This is a field guide to the twelve best off-leash dog parks in the East Bay, covering Richmond, Berkeley, Oakland, Alameda, Fremont, Newark, San Leandro and the Tri-Valley. For each park we give the address, whether dogs can legally run off-leash, whether it is fenced, hours and cost, plus the specifics that decide your afternoon: surface, shade, water, small-dog areas, winter mud and parking. Every dog rule below was verified July 2026 against the park's official city or park-district page.

Alongside the official rules, we distilled recurring themes from dog-owner reviews across Google, Yelp, Reddit, BringFido, and AllTrails — see the “What dog owners say” notes under each entry (a theme is included only when it shows up on at least two independent platforms).

How we chose these: we started with every dog park in the East Bay that had at least 100 Google reviews, kept only the ones rated 4.3 stars or higher, then ranked what was left by star rating and, where ratings tied, by number of reviews. We list them in that ranked order and did not add or drop any. Finally, we cross-checked each park's off-leash, leash, licensing and cleanup rules against its official page so the details here match the law, not just word of mouth.

Point Isabel Regional Shoreline (Richmond)

Address: 2701 Isabel St, Richmond, CA 94804 · Off-leash: yes, under voice control throughout the park · Fenced: no (open shoreline) · Hours: 5 a.m.–10 p.m. daily · Cost: free (free parking)

★ 4.8 · 2,056 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedNo (open shoreline)
Size~23 acres
SurfacePaved & dirt paths, grass
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeLimited (open meadow)
WaterBay access; dog wash on site
ParkingFree lots (fill early)

Point Isabel is about 23 acres of bayfront meadow and shoreline, and one of the few East Bay Regional Park District sites where dogs run off-leash under voice control across the whole park, not just a fenced pen. Paved and dirt paths trace the water, grassy fields open up for fetch, and dogs can wade at the bay's edge. A self-serve dog wash and a small cafe on site make it a destination rather than a quick stop — handy, because the tidal channel drops to deep, foul-smelling mud at low tide and water-loving dogs come out filthy. Check a tide table, or budget for the wash.

Two free lots off Isabel Street and Rydin Road fill fast on sunny weekend mornings, so arrive early; the regular crowd is large and generally well-socialized. Morning fog often gives way to stiff afternoon wind, and the waterline stays muddy through the rainy season. Dogs must be leashed in the parking lots and on the streets, and you must carry a six-foot leash and pick up after your dog.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Vast 23-acre shoreline where dogs can roam off-leash under voice control — regulars call it one of the biggest and best off-leash areas anywhere
  • 👍 Sweeping bay views toward the Golden Gate and Marin make the walk enjoyable for humans too
  • 👍 On-site dog wash (Mudpuppy's) and dog-friendly cafe (Sit & Stay) let you clean up a muddy dog and grab coffee without leaving the park
  • ⚠️ Gets crowded and hectic on sunny weekends, with a steady stream of dogs and people
  • ⚠️ The tidal channel turns into deep, foul-smelling mud at low tide — water-loving dogs come out filthy, so owners check tide tables or budget for the dog wash
  • ⚠️ Rainy-season visits mean muddy paths and dirty dogs

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, Adventures With Dog (blog).

Cesar Chavez Park Off-Leash Area (Berkeley)

Address: 11 Spinnaker Way, Berkeley, CA 94710 · Off-leash: yes, in the designated ~17-acre area under voice control · Fenced: no (open area, not fully enclosed) · Hours: 6 a.m.–10 p.m. · Cost: free

★ 4.7 · 1,888 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedNo (low ~32-in boundary)
Size~17 acres
SurfaceGrass & dirt
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeLittle (exposed, breezy)
WaterFountain with bowls; rinse hose
ParkingFree lot

The off-leash area covers roughly 17 acres of open grass and dirt in the north-central part of Cesar Chavez Park, on a capped former landfill with sweeping Bay Bridge and Golden Gate views. There is room to throw a frisbee full-distance without leaving the zone — ideal for dogs that love to run, less so for dogs that bolt, since only a low boundary fence separates it from sensitive habitat and the water.

Two seasonal cautions stand out. Foxtails take over the grass from late spring through summer, so check ears, eyes and paws afterward; city mowing has not solved it. And in the cooler months the city fences off a burrowing-owl protection zone, with stepped-up enforcement on dogs that stray outside the area. Keep to four dogs per handler, leash on the way in and out, and do not let dogs dig the landfill cap. There is a water fountain with bowls and a rinse hose on site.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Roughly 17 acres of open grassy space — enough room to throw a frisbee full-distance without leaving the off-leash zone
  • 👍 Panoramic bay and Golden Gate views from the waterfront paths
  • 👍 Friendly, well-behaved dog crowd and useful extras like waste-bag dispensers, a water fountain with bowls, and a rinse hose
  • ⚠️ Foxtails take over the grass in late spring and summer — owners report checking ears, eyes, and paws after every visit, and city mowing hasn't solved it
  • ⚠️ The off-leash area is essentially unfenced (only a low 32-inch boundary fence), so dogs without solid recall can wander toward sensitive habitat and trails
  • ⚠️ Ongoing tension over dogs straying outside the designated area, with stepped-up enforcement during burrowing-owl season

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, Berkeleyside.

Cubby's Dog Park (Pleasanton)

Address: 3200 W Lagoon Rd, Pleasanton, CA 94588 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced areas · Fenced: yes, separate large and small enclosures, double-gated · Hours: daily, dawn to dusk (posted hours vary; check the city page) · Cost: free

★ 4.7 · 245 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double-gated
Size~1.5 acres
SurfaceWood chips
Small-dog areaYes (separate)
ShadeThin (best mornings)
WaterFountains, wash-off hose, summer splash pad
ParkingFree lot

Cubby's is a roughly 1.5-acre fully fenced park at Bernal Community Park, named for Pleasanton's first K9 officer. Two double-gated runs separate large and small dogs, and the extras are generous: drinking fountains, a wash-off hose, agility features and a summer splash pad. The wood-chip footing drains well through the wet months, though it divides regulars who would rather have grass or dirt.

The one weak spot is shade — there are few mature trees, so afternoons get hot and regulars go early. The crowd is friendly and the dogs well-socialized. Pleasanton allows three dogs per person, leashes on and off only inside the gates, and immediate cleanup. Parking is free at the Bernal Community Park lot.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Friendly, responsible regulars and well-socialized dogs make it easy for both dogs and owners to make friends
  • 👍 Generously stocked and convenient, with free parking, poop bags, a wash-off hose, and working water fountains
  • 👍 Cleanly separated small- and large-dog sides, plus agility features and a summer dog splash pad
  • ⚠️ Shade is thin on hot afternoons, so regulars recommend morning visits and wish more trees had been planted
  • ⚠️ The wood-chip footing divides opinion, with some owners preferring grass or dirt

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Google Maps/Yelp, BringFido, DogPack, Visit Tri-Valley / local guides.

Central Park Dog Park (Fremont)

Address: 1740 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont, CA 94538 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced areas · Fenced: yes, separate large (turf) and small (grass) areas · Hours: sunrise–10 p.m. · Cost: free (some Central Park lots charge on busy summer weekends)

★ 4.6 · 863 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double-gated
SizeLarge side ~1.2 acres
SurfaceTurf (large) / grass (small)
Small-dog areaYes (small, natural grass)
ShadeShade structures
WaterDog & people fountains
ParkingPark lots (summer weekend fee)

Beside Lake Elizabeth and next to the animal shelter, this park splits into a 1.2-acre large-dog side on artificial turf, lit for early and late visits, and a smaller natural-grass side for dogs 14 inches and under at the shoulder. The turf and lights are the draw: the big side stays clean and mud-free after rain, when grass parks turn to swamp, and it works before and after work on short January days. The trade-off is the small-dog side, a few hundred square feet that can feel like an afterthought.

Both sides are double-gated, with shade structures, benches and separate dog- and people-height fountains. It fills fast on weekend mornings and holidays, so come early. Fremont checks the rules: dogs must be licensed and wear a visible tag, two per adult, with a leash carried in hand. Children 8 and under are not allowed in the off-leash area, and prong, choke and spike collars are prohibited.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Artificial-turf large-dog area stays clean and mud-free even after rain, when grass parks turn to swamp
  • 👍 Lighted and open early-to-late, so it works for before- and after-work visits
  • 👍 Spacious and generally clean, with shade structures, benches, and separate people- and dog-height water fountains
  • ⚠️ The small-dog side is tiny — a few hundred square feet of natural grass that feels like an afterthought
  • ⚠️ Fills up fast on weekend mornings and holidays; regulars advise arriving early to beat the crowd

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, DogPack, TripAdvisor.

Alameda Dog Park (Alameda)

Address: 2990 Main St, Alameda, CA 94501 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced area · Fenced: yes, fully fenced single run · Hours: park hours (roughly dawn to dusk) · Cost: free

★ 4.6 · 800 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, single run
SizeLong, narrow
SurfaceDecomposed granite
Small-dog areaNo (all sizes together)
ShadeLittle
WaterNone reliable — bring your own
ParkingFree street/ferry lot

This is the Main Street Dog Park on Alameda's West End, beside the Main Street ferry terminal. It is a long, fully fenced single run open to all sizes, with a decomposed-granite surface and estuary views of passing ships and the Oakland port cranes. The length lets dogs sprint back and forth, and it is usually quiet — a calm choice for a dog that finds busy parks overwhelming.

Two things to pack for: there is no reliable running water, so bring your own jugs and bowls, and there is little shade on hot afternoons. Keep a leash in hand and leash up while entering and exiting; dogs must wear an ID tag or be microchipped, be current on shots, and females in heat are not allowed. Street parking near the terminal is free.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Roomy and rarely crowded with separate small- and large-dog areas, a calm alternative to busier local parks
  • 👍 Scenic, breezy shoreline setting with bay and Oakland-crane views next to Crown Beach
  • ⚠️ Sandy footing tracks into shoes, with regulars suggesting boots over sneakers
  • ⚠️ Little shade and no reliable drinking water on site, so owners are advised to bring their own

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, Foursquare, DogTrekker.

Dog Park at Lower Washington Park (Alameda)

Address: Lower Washington Park (near Westline Dr & Otis Dr), Alameda, CA 94501 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced area · Fenced: yes, separate small-dog and large-dog areas · Hours: park hours (roughly dawn to dusk) · Cost: free

★ 4.6 · 680 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double-gated
Sizenot listed
SurfaceSand & dirt
Small-dog areaYes (separate, shaded)
ShadeShaded small-dog side
WaterYes (drinking water)
ParkingFree

Alameda's second dog park sits in Lower Washington Park, steps from Robert Crown Memorial Beach, with separate double-gated runs for small and large dogs. It is clean and well-tended, and the shaded small-dog side comes with donated lawn chairs, drinking water and a communal stash of tennis balls. The surface is sandy, so diggers and fetchers come home coated in sand and dust.

The big-dog side gets crowded after work and on weekends; regulars decamp to quieter parks at peak. The rules mirror Main Street — keep a leash in hand, stay in the run and within view of your dog, and leash up while entering and exiting — and dogs need current vaccinations and an ID tag or chip. Remember dogs must be leashed on the beach itself. Parking is free.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Separate fenced big-dog and small-dog areas with double-gated entries, steps from Crown Beach
  • 👍 Easy free parking and a clean, well-tended feel with garbage cans and scoopers on hand
  • 👍 Shaded small-dog side with donated lawn chairs, drinking water, and a stash of communal tennis balls and toys
  • ⚠️ Sandy surface — dogs that dig or fetch come home coated in sand and dust
  • ⚠️ The big-dog side gets crowded at peak after-work and weekend hours; some locals decamp to quieter parks

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, Foursquare.

Muirwood Dog Park (Pleasanton)

Address: 4701 Muirwood Dr, Pleasanton, CA 94588 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced areas · Fenced: yes, two enclosures including a small/shy-dog area · Hours: 7 a.m.–8 p.m. · Cost: free

★ 4.6 · 339 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, two enclosures
Sizenot listed
SurfaceWood chips
Small-dog areaYes (small/shy/senior)
ShadeGood (well-shaded)
WaterWater stations
ParkingLot; restrooms in adjacent park

Muirwood Community Park has two fenced enclosures, one reserved for small, elderly or shy dogs — a real option if your dog is easily overwhelmed. It is consistently rated among the Tri-Valley's cleanest and best-shaded runs, with wood-chip footing, water stations, tables and chairs, and restrooms in the adjacent community park. Walking tracks and trails wrap the grounds, so you can stretch the visit into a longer loop.

It is tucked into a residential neighborhood and easy to miss the first time, and noticeably busier on weekends than the mellow weekday scene. Pleasanton's rules are the same as at Cubby's: three dogs per person, and pick up waste immediately. It is free and rarely as crowded as the newer Cubby's.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Consistently praised as one of the Tri-Valley's cleanest and best-shaded dog parks
  • 👍 Separate fenced enclosures for large and small/senior/shy dogs, with wood-chip footing
  • 👍 Well-equipped: water stations, chairs and tables, poop bags, and restrooms in the adjacent community park
  • ⚠️ Tucked into a residential neighborhood and easy to miss on a first visit
  • ⚠️ Noticeably busier on weekends than the mellow weekday scene

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, DogTrekker, Foursquare, Nextdoor.

Newbark Dog Park (Newark)

Address: 35501 Cedar Blvd, Newark, CA 94560 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced enclosure · Fenced: yes, separate small and large areas, double-gated · Hours: sunrise–sunset · Cost: free

★ 4.6 · 273 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double-gated
Size~1 acre
SurfaceGrass & concrete
Small-dog areaYes (under 30 lb)
ShadePergola & trees
WaterYes (dogs & owners)
ParkingAmple

Newbark is a roughly one-acre fully fenced park inside Newark Community Park, with a staging area at the entry and a separate small-dog side for dogs under 30 pounds. A large pergola and trees give real shade — not a given at newer parks — alongside seating, water and waste bags. Both sides are double-gated.

Upkeep can slip on a bad day, with reports of uncleared waste, overgrown grass or puddles on the concrete, but the regulars are attentive and the dogs generally friendly. Under the Newark Municipal Code, dogs must be licensed, vaccinated and under an adult handler's control, handlers are limited to two dogs, and waste must be bagged and binned. Unleash in the staging area before entering the main run. Parking is ample.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Ample parking and clearly separated sides for small (under 30 lb) and large dogs
  • 👍 A large pergola and trees provide real shade, with seating, water, and waste bags on hand
  • 👍 Attentive, welcoming regulars and generally friendly dogs
  • ⚠️ Upkeep can slip, with reports of uncleared waste, overgrown grass, and puddles or urine on the concrete on poorly maintained days

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, DogPack, DogDog.

Joaquin Miller Dog Play Area (Oakland)

Address: 3590 Sanborn Dr, Oakland, CA 94602 · Off-leash: yes, but only inside the fenced Dog Play Area · Fenced: yes, separate large and small sections · Hours: park hours (roughly sunrise to dusk) · Cost: free

★ 4.6 · 253 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, separate large & small
Sizenot listed
SurfaceWood chips (no grass)
Small-dog areaYes (separate)
ShadeAmple (redwoods)
WaterFountain
ParkingEasy, close to gates

This fenced Dog Play Area on Sanborn Drive is the one place in Joaquin Miller Park where dogs come off leash — Oakland's municipal code keeps the rest of the park and every trail leash-only. It has separate large- and small-dog sections, benches, waste stations and a water fountain, set on a shaded, forested hillside among the redwoods.

The hillside setting keeps it cool on hot days but slow to dry after winter rain, and the footing is wood chips rather than grass — the city is slow to replenish them, especially on the small-dog side. Owners also flag the occasional poorly controlled dog whose handler does not step in. Parking is easy and close to the gates, and a leashed hike on the surrounding trails pairs well.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Two separate fenced sections for large and small dogs, with benches and waste stations
  • 👍 Shaded, forested hillside setting keeps it cool on hot days
  • 👍 Friendly regulars and easy parking close to the enclosures
  • ⚠️ No grass — just wood chips that the city is slow to replenish, especially on the small-dog side
  • ⚠️ Recurring reports of poorly controlled or aggressive dogs whose owners don't intervene

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, Wanderlog, TripAdvisor.

Walnut Creek Dog Park at Heather Farm Park (Walnut Creek)

Address: north end of Heather Farm Park, N San Carlos Dr, Walnut Creek, CA 94598 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced area · Fenced: yes, separate large and small/senior areas, double-gated · Hours: 8 a.m.–dusk daily, except Thursdays noon–dusk · Cost: free

★ 4.5 · 535 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double-gated
Size~1 acre
SurfaceReal grass
Small-dog areaYes (small/senior, under 30 lb)
ShadeShaded benches
WaterFountains & buckets
ParkingNearby; restrooms close

At the north end of Heather Farm Park, this one-acre fenced park has real grass, professionally cleaned and maintained weekly, which keeps it in better shape than most dog-park lawns. A separate side serves small and senior dogs (under 30 pounds), both sides enter through double gates, and there are water fountains, buckets and shaded benches, with restrooms and parking close by.

Two things catch first-timers out. The dog park opens late, at noon, on Thursdays for maintenance. And the rules are enforced: no more than three dogs per adult, dogs at least four months old, current on vaccinations and free of parasites. The recurring gripe is inattentive owners — waste left behind and rough play that goes uncorrected — so keep an eye on your own dog. Leash and unleash only inside the double-gated area.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Real grass — a fenced one-acre area with a separate side for small and senior dogs
  • 👍 Well-supplied with water fountains, buckets, and shaded benches
  • 👍 Professionally cleaned and maintained weekly, which keeps the grass in better shape than most dog parks
  • ⚠️ Inattentive owners are a recurring gripe — waste left behind and rough play that goes uncorrected
  • ⚠️ Occasional run-ins with aggressive dogs whose owners won't remove them
  • ⚠️ Closed Thursday mornings for maintenance, which catches first-time visitors off guard

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, WanderBoat.

Ohlone Dog Park (Berkeley)

Address: 1800 Hearst Ave, Berkeley, CA 94703 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced area · Fenced: yes, separate small and large areas · Hours: park hours (roughly 6 a.m.–10 p.m.) · Cost: free

★ 4.5 · 424 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double-gate entry
SizeCompact
SurfaceWood chips & dirt
Small-dog areaYes (separate)
ShadeMature trees
WaterYes; waste bins
ParkingStreet; near North Berkeley BART

Ohlone has a strong claim to being the oldest off-leash dog park in the United States: neighbors began using the parcel as a dog run in 1979, and the City of Berkeley officially designated it in 1983. It is a compact, community-run run inside the larger Ohlone Park, with separate double-gated areas for small and large dogs, mature trees for shade, running water and waste bins. The footing is wood chips and dirt, dusty when dry and muddy when wet.

It works best as a sociable neighborhood park rather than a place to let a dog really stretch out, and it is an easy walk from North Berkeley BART. Worth knowing: the surrounding Ohlone Park has drawn encampment and public-safety concerns near the run. Dogs must be leashed until inside the fence, licensed, and vaccinated against rabies, and aggressive dogs are not allowed.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Beloved historic park (billed as the world's first off-leash dog park) with a genuinely social, chatty owner community
  • 👍 Mature trees for shade, running water, and waste stations, with separate areas for shy and confident dogs
  • 👍 Central, walkable location close to North Berkeley BART
  • ⚠️ Bark-and-dirt footing gets dusty when dry and muddy in wet weather
  • ⚠️ The surrounding Ohlone Park has drawn encampment, trash, and public-safety concerns near the dog run

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, DogPack, Wheree.

Marina Dog Park (San Leandro)

Address: 14001 Monarch Bay Dr, San Leandro, CA 94577 · Off-leash: yes, inside the fenced area · Fenced: yes, with a separate small-dog section · Hours: park hours (roughly dawn to dusk) · Cost: free

★ 4.5 · 277 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, separate sections
Size58,000 sq ft
SurfaceGravel (no grass)
Small-dog areaYes (25 lb & under)
ShadeShade structures (windy, limited natural)
WaterFaucets
ParkingEasy (lot)

Marina Dog Park is a 58,000-square-foot fenced run in San Leandro's Marina Park, near the shoreline, with a designated small-dog section for dogs 25 pounds and under at the north end. It is one of the larger enclosed parks on this list, with shade structures, picnic benches and water faucets. There is no grass — the surface is gravel, which drains well and makes cleanup easy but can scratch small dogs' undersides, so it suits bigger dogs better.

The bayside spot is often windy with limited natural shade, so it is worth double-checking the gate latches behind you. Under the San Leandro Municipal Code you must carry leashes at all times inside, remove choke, pinch or pronged collars, and keep to no more than three dogs per person. Dogs must be healthy, vaccinated, licensed, over four months old and not in heat.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Clean and well-drained with no grass, which many owners find makes cleanup easier, plus a working water fountain
  • 👍 Easy parking, ample seating and shade structures, and separate small- and large-dog sections
  • 👍 Scenic shoreline setting alongside the wider Marina Park amenities
  • ⚠️ The exposed shoreline location is often windy with limited natural shade
  • ⚠️ Rocky/gravel footing can scratch small dogs' undersides, making it better suited to bigger dogs

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, DogPack, Tripadvisor, City of San Leandro.

Know Before You Go

  • Leash up outside the off-leash zone. Every park here requires dogs on a six-foot leash in parking lots, on connecting paths and outside the designated area, even at voice-control parks like Point Isabel and Cesar Chavez.
  • Voice control is a legal standard. At East Bay Regional Park District sites such as Point Isabel, and at Berkeley's waterfront, an off-leash dog must stay in sight and return immediately when called, and you must carry a leash for each dog.
  • Keep licenses and vaccinations current. Most city parks (Fremont, Alameda, Newark, Walnut Creek, Berkeley, San Leandro) require a current dog license, an ID tag or microchip, and up-to-date rabies and other vaccinations.
  • Mind the dog limits. Handler limits are common, usually two or three dogs per person (four at Cesar Chavez). Professional walkers often need a permit; EBRPD requires one for walking more than three dogs.
  • Clean up every time and don't dig. Bag and bin waste at every park, and keep dogs from digging, which is specifically prohibited on the capped-landfill parks like Cesar Chavez and Point Isabel.
  • Watch seasonal and maintenance closures. Cesar Chavez fences off a burrowing-owl protection zone in the cooler months, and the Heather Farm dog park opens late (noon) on Thursdays for maintenance.
  • Small or shy dogs have options. Cubby's, Central Park, Muirwood, Newbark, Lower Washington, Joaquin Miller in Oakland, Ohlone, Heather Farm and Marina all have separate small-dog areas.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which East Bay dog parks let dogs run off-leash without a fence?

Point Isabel Regional Shoreline in Richmond and the Cesar Chavez Park off-leash area in Berkeley are the two big unfenced options. At both, dogs may be off-leash only under voice control, meaning they stay in sight and come back immediately when called, and you must carry a leash. If your dog does not have a solid recall, a fully fenced park is the safer choice.

Are these dog parks free?

Yes. All twelve parks are free to enter. Parking is free at Point Isabel and most city parks. The main exception to watch is Fremont's Central Park, where some lots can charge a parking fee on busy summer weekends, though the dog park itself is free.

Do I need a license or vaccinations to use them?

For most city-run parks, yes. Fremont, Alameda, Newark, Walnut Creek, Berkeley and San Leandro all require dogs to be licensed, wear an ID tag or be microchipped, and be current on rabies and other vaccinations. Even where a tag is not checked at the gate, keeping vaccinations current protects your dog around others.

Which parks are best for small dogs?

Look for a dedicated small-dog enclosure: Cubby's and Muirwood in Pleasanton, Central Park in Fremont, Newbark in Newark, the Lower Washington park in Alameda, Joaquin Miller in Oakland, Ohlone in Berkeley, Heather Farm in Walnut Creek, and Marina in San Leandro all separate small dogs from large dogs.

Can puppies use these parks?

Wait until your puppy is fully vaccinated, and check each park's minimum age. Heather Farm, for example, requires dogs to be at least four months old, and every park requires current vaccinations. Until then, stick to controlled, one-on-one socialization rather than a busy off-leash park.
